hypothesis.count_consequence: Count-NEUTRAL, and that is the discriminant. Ours and the target both stand at 104 instructions with an IDENTICAL opcode multiset and an IDENTICAL slot map, so the six conversions already exist in both streams in the same number and the same kinds. Any form that moves the count in EITHER direction has left this hypothesis and hit a different mechanism -- as PROBE 4 did (O101, the CSE collapsed to one load) and PROBE 2 did (fnmsubs traded for fmsubs). A cure here reassigns two blocks of stack offsets and changes nothing else.

hypothesis.statement: The whole remaining residual is carried by the SIX s32 staging doubles at r1+64..r1+108, and it is a BLOCK SWAP, not a layout error: the slot map is IDENTICAL (target 21 slots, ours 21, frame 136/136) and each axis's three temps are contiguous in both streams, but the x-axis block sits at 64/72/80 in the target and at 88/96/104 in ours, with the y-axis block taking the other half. Within each block the order is the same in both (divisor conversion, dividend conversion, then the centered term's (f64) conversion), so exactly one bit differs: which axis owns the low block. That single bit accounts for 16 of the 17 IMMEDIATE words. The BASELINE source had this bit CORRECT (x-block low) while missing the save pair; every state that HAS the save pair has it wrong, so the two may be coupled. The next lane's step 1 is the CONVERSION-SPELLING class, the one class not yet measured that plausibly reaches codegen here, because it is what creates and orders these six temps: rewrite the centered terms as `lbl_80348B28 * (f64)(f32)viewport->w` (and the h twin), and separately bind the divisions' conversions in the opposite operand order. Do NOT re-probe statement order, declaration order or the pad type: all three are measured dead below with byte-identical objects.
